reasons: Correctly identifies a genuine deviation: the 'unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One' carve-out flips ownership of Corio-created interface coding to the vendor with no licence back, which contradicts the preferred position (Customer owns deliverables/work product) and edges toward the walk-away (assignment of Customer IP to Vendor).

Redline reaches the playbook position: the ownership flip is deleted so Developments are 'owned by Corio', and the commercial rationale is preserved by a narrow nonexclusive, royalty-free support licence to Commerce One - a proportionate concession, not a new exposure.

Edit is textually clean: the dangling 'including / intellectual property rights in the Developments.' fragment spanning p0115-p0116 is removed without leaving orphaned text, and Commerce One's retained ownership of its pre-existing materials and the Software itself is untouched, consistent with 'Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine'.

The added sentence supplies the Customer Data ownership confirmation the rule requires and expressly negates any assignment of such data or Developments to the vendor; the deterministic check confirming no residual assignment of our IP/data passes.

The failed 'minimal edit p0115' ratio is advisory only here - the rule requires excising the ownership-flip clause and substituting licence language, so the higher changed-character ratio is justified; the surrounding operative text is otherwise preserved verbatim.

Comment is accurate, correctly scoped to Section 13.5, uses the required prefix and concise first-person-plural tone, and explains both changes without overstating. Minor drafting nit for the negotiator: the new sentence references 'the MarketSite.net Service', which is not among the resolved definitions - confirm that defined term exists or delete the reference.
